issues.detail: The Hebrew 'אִישׁ עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה' means 'a man working the ground/soil' (a farmer), but the Vietnamese renders it as 'một người làm ruộng' (a field worker) which is acceptable, yet the final clause 'כִּי אָדָם הִקְנַנִי מִנְּעוּרָי' means 'for a man acquired me from my youth' (i.e., someone bought/owned me as a servant from youth), but the Vietnamese says 'người ta đã bắt tôi làm nghề chăn nuôi' ('people made me do the livestock-raising trade'), which adds the concept of being forced into livestock raising—a substantive addition not present in the Hebrew, which only states being acquired/owned, not forced into a specific occupation.
